chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about two men who shared a slave, and one of them freed his share, so he said:
"If it causes harm, he is compelled to free the entire slave; otherwise, the slave is asked for the value of the other half."

key_terms.اُسْتُسْعِيَ: He is asked for the money/value (to redeem)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one of two partners frees his share of a shared slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'idrar' (harm) in partial manumission, ensuring the freed slave's dignity is preserved. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing economic or social detriment to the remaining share, distinguishing between forced full emancipation and voluntary redemption by the slave.
